sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 26.0% a year from $4.32 billion in FY2016 to $34.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F231].
The path was two step changes rather than a smooth climb: revenue rose 68.3% in FY2021 and 43.6% in FY2022, then fell 3.9% in FY2023 before rebounding 34.3% in FY2025 [D258][D314][D370][D483].
The FY2022 jump included the Xilinx acquisition, which brought Embedded revenue from $246 million in FY2021 to $4.55 billion in FY2022 [S109][S110][P41].
FY2023's decline came from a 25% drop in Client revenue on weak PC demand and inventory correction, partly offset by Embedded's full-year Xilinx contribution [P35].
In FY2025 Data Center contributed 15.7pp of the 34.3% revenue growth and Client and Gaming 19.0pp, while Embedded subtracted 0.4pp [D694][D701][D731][D483].
Data Center revenue rose 32% on strong demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPU accelerators, and Client and Gaming rose 51% on Ryzen processors, semi-custom console SoCs and Radeon GPUs [P15].
Data Center was 48.0% of FY2025 revenue, so the largest segment is also the most concentrated [D692].
Operating income grew 94.4% against revenue growth of 34.3%, an incremental operating margin of 20.3% [D484][D483][D511].
Operating costs grew 10.0pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 24.3% [D512][D504].
Gross margin of 49.5% is the window high, above the 44.7% median, and operating margin of 10.7% sits above its 7.2% median but far below the 22.2% FY2021 high [F40][D800][D801][F60][D795][D794].
FY2025 gross margin rose 0.2pp as product mix improved, partly offset by about $440 million of MI308 inventory and related charges tied to U.S. export controls [D498][P14].
The FY2025 operating margin rose 3.3pp, with cost of revenue adding 0.2pp, R&D 1.7pp and other lines 2.6pp, while SG&A subtracted 1.2pp [D499][D513][D514][D516][D515].
Net margin of 12.5% sat 1.9pp above the 10.7% operating margin, helped by $577 million of other income and a $103 million tax benefit [F80][F60][D843][X123][X113].

Operating cash flow of $7.71 billion was 1.78x net income of $4.34 billion, above the 1.61x window median, and free cash flow of $6.74 billion was 1.55x net income [F110][F70][D470][D833][F130][D471].
FY2025 operating cash flow was driven by net income plus $4.6 billion of non-cash adjustments, partly offset by a $2.2 billion inventory build to ramp Data Center products [P3].
Free cash flow margin of 19.4% is near the 19.6% window high and above the 6.5% median, while capex of $974 million was 2.8% of revenue and 1.87x D&A [D467][D803][D804][F120][D466][D472].

Net cash rose to $6.46 billion, or 18.6% of revenue, from $3.41 billion a year earlier, and ranks at the 100th percentile of five semis peers against a -17.3% peer median [D476][D477][D419][D844][D845].
Total debt rose 138% to $4.10 billion as AMD issued $1.5 billion of notes in March 2025, lifting interest expense to $131 million [D475][D508][P6][X93].
Buybacks of $1.32 billion were 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was flat at -0.1% [D478][D479][D506].
Revenue fell 3.9% in FY2023, the only decline in the window, on a 25% Client drop and 9% Gaming drop [D370][P35].
The decline was cyclical PC and console inventory correction rather than structural, since revenue grew 13.7% and 34.3% in the two following years [D426][D483].
Total debt rose 138% in FY2025 to $4.10 billion from $1.72 billion [D475][D418].
The increase is modest against $10.6 billion of cash and investments, so leverage is not a balance-sheet concern [D474].
The effective tax rate moved -21.3pp in FY2025 to -2.5%, driven by an $853 million benefit from release of uncertain tax positions [D469][D412][P4].
The benefit is one-time, so FY2025 net margin of 12.5% overstates the recurring tax-adjusted earnings base [F80].
Whether Data Center revenue growth holds above the FY2025 32.2% rate, or decelerates toward the FY2023 7.5% level, in the FY2026 10-K [D693][D687].
Whether operating margin holds above the 7.2% window median or falls back toward the FY2023 1.8% trough, in the FY2026 10-K [D795][F58].
Whether free cash flow margin stays near the 19.6% window high or drops toward the 6.5% median as inventory days of 165 unwind, in the FY2026 10-K [D803][D804][D481].
